analysis:
Examined the provider streaming handler (ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift, head lines 624-1538) and the SSE parser (ProviderLoop+SSEParser.swift). The PR changes the tool-call type from OpenAIToolCall to OpenAIToolCallDelta so streamed fragments are handled. It adds a `deliveredText` accumulator (lines 1064-1068, 1167, 1179, 1185-1187) of visible output only: content, reasoning, tool names and argument text. That accumulator is used as the cancelled-stream billing floor, `deliveredCompletionTokenFloor` at line 1362. Tool-call fragments are still folded into `fullResponseText` through `encodeToolCallsForHash` and into the response hash/SE signature (lines 1184, 1494-1499), one marker per fragment in wire order. This is an integrity-neutral change: the hash covers what was emitted, and an empty-name or argument fragment still counts as content.

Security controls are intact. Response encryption stays fail-closed: `emitSSE` sends an encryptionFailure terminal and aborts, so no plaintext leaves (T-008). Cancellation still propagates (T-010). The prefix-cache receipt and scope logic is unchanged (T-041). The change affects the provider-side billing floor and attestation hash only. The hash remains provider-self-reported (T-007 accepted).

Residual unverified contracts: the OpenAIToolCallDelta type definition in the MLXLMServer dependency (optional `function.name`/`arguments`, Encodable and Equatable conformance) and the `StreamedGenerationUsage` struct's new `deliveredCompletionTokenFloor` parameter (line 1362). Neither is in the supplied evidence. They are outside this diff and should be checked at integration. No concrete regression was identified.
